body: I tested it on some of my own projects and was able to confirm the problem. Details: * Browsers tested: _Firefox 150.0.2_ and _Chromium 147.0.7723.0_. * Shadows disabled. * Exported without debugging. * Tested with and without enabling `application/run/low_processor_mode`. * I waited more than a minute to make sure the rendering was stable before taking the screenshots. |~29fps with `scaling_3d_scale=0.5`|~51fps with `scaling_3d_scale=1.0`| | --- | --- | | | |
I can reproduce, but only on Windows. On my Linux machine the scale doesn't impact performance at all.
As a web developer by day, I have a sneaking suspicion this is a browser side issue and not a Godot issue.

I tested again on the same machine, but booted Ubuntu 26.04 instead of Windows 11, and the issue disappeared. I saw the same behavior on an Intel N100 mini-PC: a huge performance drop on Windows 11, while it works fine on Fedora 44.

Based on my tests, the issue does not occur on Linux (AMD/Intel GPUs), iPhones, Apple Silicon MacBooks, or a Snapdragon-based Android 10 phone.

On Windows, the issue is consistent across different browsers (Firefox and Chrome) and across both Intel and AMD GPUs.

I haven’t been able to test NVIDIA GPUs on Linux, but the issue is present on Windows.

| Platform / OS | Hardware | Browser(s) Tested | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows 11 | AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT | Firefox, Chrome | ❌ Performance tanks | FPS drops from 160 to ~27 when Scaling3D scale is set below 1.0 on a 4K monitor. CPU usage increases dramatically. |
| Windows 11 | NVIDIA RTX 4070 | Opera (Chromium) | ❌ Performance tanks | FPS drops from 180 to ~35 when Scaling3D scale is set below 1.0 on an ultra wide monitor. |
| Windows 11 | Intel N100 mini-PC | Firefox, Edge (Chromium) | ❌ Performance tanks | Same severe slowdown observed as on AMD desktop system. |
| Windows 10 | Intel MacBook with AMD GPU | Chrome | ❌ Performance tanks | Same issue reproduced under Windows 10 on Intel MacBook hardware with AMD GPU. |
| Ubuntu 26.04 | AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT | Firefox | ✅ Works correctly | Issue disappears completely on Linux. |
| Fedora 44 | Intel N100 mini-PC | Firefox, Opera (Chromium) | ✅ Works correctly | Runs faster when Scaling3D scale below 1.0. |
| macOS 12 | Intel MacBook with AMD GPU | Safari, Chrome | ✅ Works correctly | Runs faster when Scaling3D scale below 1.0. |
| iPhone | Apple mobile GPU | Safari | ✅ Works correctly | Runs faster when Scaling3D scale below 1.0. |
| Apple Silicon MacBook | Apple Silicon GPU (M4 Pro) | Safari, Chrome | ✅ Works correctly | No issue observed. |
| Android 10 | Snapdragon 845 | Chrome | ✅ Works correctly | Runs faster when Scaling3D scale below 1.0. |
| Android 11 | Exynos 9609 | Chrome | ✅ Works correctly | Runs faster when Scaling3D scale below 1.0. |
| NVIDIA GPU Linux systems | NVIDIA GPUs on Linux | Not tested | ⚪ Unknown | No Linux with NVIDIA hardware available for testing. |

The other computer, which has an RTX 4070, is my friend’s desktop PC with the monitor connected directly to the NVIDIA GPU, so I assumed his i5-9600K’s iGPU would not be handling the displayed graphics.
This is happening to me on Windows 11, Godot 4.7, Chrome 152, 5070 Ti with 610.88 drivers, and without any iGPU.

I was doing some testing on this issue to create my own bug report, but just found this one, so I'll share my findings here.

@clayjohn  This issue seems to be a regression starting in Godot 4.5 Beta 1 and onward, previous versions (4.5 Dev 4 and prior) don't have the same problem. Between 4.5 Dev 4 and 4.5 Beta 1, there was a news post called "[Upcoming (serious) Web performance boost](https://godotengine.org/article/upcoming-serious-web-performance-boost/)", it could be coincidence, but maybe a change was made then that caused the bug?

As for the systems I tested it on, I've only been able to reproduce the problem on Windows. Unfortunately, I haven't tested any Linux systems with an Nvidia GPU so I can't contribute on that front just yet.

I played a bit with this and in my case this is happening only in fullscreen. When the game is inline in a webpage, the scaling is working fine, but once in fullscreen the FPS drops.

Just tried it on a Linux system with an Nvidia card (Ubuntu 24.04 + Quadro K1200) and can confirm that the issue does not occur. I know it's a workstation card and not a typical gaming card, but I'm leaning towards this being a bug in Windows with all the data.
